card.name: Clause boundaries in general web prose
card.fires_on: Sentence-ending periods and small connecting words (order, though, that, One) in ordinary non-drug web prose, where a new clause or sentence is about to begin.

modes.label: Sentence-final period
modes.description: A full stop closing a sentence in expository text, just before the next sentence elaborates on it.
modes.example: Federal employment discrimination laws<<.>> It prohibits discrimination in any aspect of employment

modes.label: Linking word mid-sentence
modes.description: A connector such as order, though, or that that introduces a purpose or contrast clause.
modes.example: To implement these designs,<< though>>, it is necessary to have new techniques

card.writes: Weak signal; it slightly favors words like differing, being, employing and thus, which continue a sentence with a comparison or consequence.
card.plain: It marks spots in everyday prose where one clause ends or a connecting word leads into the next idea.
